claim_evidence.claim_text: The selected immutable Hermes boundary is canonical repository `NousResearch/hermes-agent`, annotated tag `v2026.7.7.2`, tag object `b7751df34688835a108e0d630f3495fc11f3df79`, dereferenced commit `9de9c25f620ff7f1ce0fd5457d596052d5159596`, package version `0.18.2`; GitHub published the release on 2026-07-08.

The pinned repository contains a concrete agent harness/runtime with CLI, gateway, ACP, batch/API/library entry points feeding `AIAgent`, plus prompt/provider/tool machinery, session persistence, cron, plugins, skills, documentation, and tests; it is suitable for the existing implementation case method.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Hermes and OpenClaw have different Git roots, and Hermes later added an OpenClaw migration that translates selected persona, memory, instruction, skill, model/provider, behavior, session, MCP, messaging, approval, browser, and secret state while archiving unsupported concepts.

claim_evidence.claim_text: The defensible relationship classification is separately rooted repositories with later migration compatibility and selective documented influence—not direct whole-repository descent and not independent convergence.

On 2026-07-18, GitHub reported 216,532 stars, 40,588 forks, 836 subscribers, 23,538 open issues, and Nous Research organization ownership for `NousResearch/hermes-agent`; these are repository-attention and metadata signals, not user, deployment, team-size, quality, or effectiveness evidence.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for snapshot, low applicability to adoption

claim_evidence.claim_text: At the selected commit, Hermes history contains 14,857 reachable commits, 2,014 `git shortlog -sne` identities, 3,953 commits at or after 2026-06-08T00:00:00Z, 11,391 at or after 2026-04-08T00:00:00Z, and 21 version tags from `v2026.3.12` through `v2026.7.7.2`; these establish continuity and activity, not users or team size.

Select Hermes as the final pre-Checkpoint-3 case and defer Browser Use until after the first learning-oriented synthesis: Hermes offers high comparative and teaching value, while the accepted cost is less architectural breadth and an explicitly unresolved perception-grounded R5/R6 gap.

claim_evidence.claim_text: The future case should ask how Hermes connects models to users and environments and, only where pinned evidence supports comparison, which OpenClaw concepts are translated, selectively borrowed, deliberately unmapped, or independently implemented and what tradeoffs follow.

After maintainer review of Hermes, convene Checkpoint 3 immediately, then create the first cross-harness synthesis and derive learning material from reviewed evidence; add no other implementation before that checkpoint and reopen Browser Use later against explicit gaps.
